concepts.def: IBDP DT uses analysing, designing, planning, creating, evaluating; iterative loops repeat as understanding develops.
Identifies user needs through observation, interviews and PMI charts; benchmarks against existing solutions.
Quantitative and qualitative criteria covering function, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials, cost, sustainability; agreed before design.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Final Production — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Final Production brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Final Production.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a timber is a hardwood or softwood?
options: Current stays the same.
Whether the wood itself is physically hard or soft.
How long the tree took to grow.
The type of tree - deciduous (hardwood) or coniferous (softwood), not its hardness.

mcqs.q: If voltage is doubled and resistance is unchanged, what happens to the current?
options: Current doubles (V = IR, so I = V/R).
Current halves.
Current stays the same.
